title: Self-hosting architecture
description: Map Tixkit applications, durable services, trust boundaries, and public ingress before deployment.
body: Tixkit runs separate API, Temporal worker, admin, checkout, and documentation processes. PostgreSQL is the primary documented local path; repository validation also covers declared compatible database modes. Redis supports runtime coordination, Temporal owns durable workflows, and S3 compatible storage owns generated/uploaded artifacts. Trust boundaries Expose only required public ingress: buyer checkout/public API, authenticated admin/API, provider webhooks, and documentation. Keep database, Redis, Temporal service, and object storage administration private. The API authenticates and scopes requests. The worker consumes trusted Temporal tasks but still calls scoped repositories/providers. Browser applications never receive database, provider, API key, or signing secrets. Failure boundaries API health does not prove worker readiness; worker health does not prove provider readiness. Monitor each service plus database, Redis, Temporal, storage, authentication, payments, messaging, and webhook delivery independently. Continue with configuration and secrets /self hosting/configuration .

title: Configure authentication
description: Choose and validate the supported authentication provider without weakening tenant or session boundaries.
body: The repository supports its documented local development principal and provider backed authentication paths. Local authentication is for controlled development; do not expose it as a production login mechanism. Provider setup Configure the provider's public browser key and server secret in their correct runtime boundaries. Set the matching AUTH PROVIDER and browser provider selection values, then restart API and admin applications. Provider organization identity must resolve to Tixkit tenant/organization context. Test suspended users, missing organization membership, multi tenant selection, expired sessions, and forbidden actions. Safe migration Follow the provider migration procedure for identity mapping and rollback. Never silently create cross tenant memberships from an unverified email match. Keep the prior path available until login, logout, session refresh, organization selection, and API authorization pass in the target environment.

title: Back up and restore Tixkit
description: Protect relational data and object artifacts with measured, rehearsed recovery procedures.
body: Backups are not complete until a restore rehearsal proves usable application state. Protect database data and required object storage artifacts; document which ephemeral Redis/Temporal state is reconstructed and which durable Temporal persistence is protected by its own service plan. Backup Run the repository's engine/object storage backup procedures with encrypted destinations, least privilege access, retention, and monitoring. Record timestamps and non secret artifact identifiers. Compact operators use bun run compact:backup and bun run compact:restore . The Compact runbook /self hosting/compact defines the artifact contents, checksum gate, and Temporal volume boundary. Restore rehearsal Restore into an isolated environment, run migrations only as required by the target commit, start API/worker/application processes, and verify tenant scope, a representative event/order, artifact download, workflow visibility, and health checks. Measure recovery point and recovery time from actual rehearsal evidence. Do not publish invented RPO/RTO claims.

title: Run the Compact profile
description: Start, operate, back up, restore, upgrade, and remove a complete single-host Tixkit installation.
body: Compact is the supported single host profile for evaluation and smaller installations. It runs the API, worker, admin dashboard, checkout, migrations, seeded evaluation data, PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal, Temporal UI, and S3 compatible object storage. It is not highly available and does not run MySQL alongside its default PostgreSQL database. Host envelope Use a 64 bit Linux host or Docker Desktop with at least 4 CPU cores, 8 GiB of memory, and 30 GiB of free disk. Building all application images is resource intensive; 8 cores, 16 GiB of memory, and 60 GiB of free disk is the recommended starting envelope. Measure your own event, checkout, workflow, media, and retention load before production use. Move to the Production profile when you need multiple hosts, independent scaling, managed backing services, availability guarantees, or formal disaster recovery objectives. First start From the repository root: compact:init writes infra/compact/.env with mode 0600 and unique persistent service and signing secrets. It refuses to overwrite an existing file. Back up this file separately; do not commit or share it. compact:up builds the application images, applies idempotent migrations, creates the object bucket, seeds an evaluation organization and event, and waits for every service health condition. The default endpoints are: checkout: http://localhost:3000 admin: http://localhost:3001 API readiness: http://localhost:4000/ready Temporal UI: http://localhost:8080 MinIO console: http://localhost:9001 Edit the non secret PORT values in infra/compact/.env before compact:up when a host port is already occupied. Frontend API URLs are baked into their images, so rerun compact:up after changing API PORT . Operate Restarting the host or Docker preserves the four named data volumes. Running bun run compact:up again rechecks migrations, storage initialization, seed idempotency, and service health. Back up and restore The backup quiesces the application and workflow tier, then captures the application database, both Temporal databases, and owned object storage as one logical snapshot. Its manifest records the Tixkit version, source commit, byte counts, and SHA 256 checksums. Restore verifies the exact artifact set, checksums, version, and archive entry safety, restores into temporary databases and a temporary bucket, and validates their required schemas before cutover. It retains rollback databases and objects until the complete profile is healthy. Keep backup directories and infra/compact/.env encrypted outside the host's failure domain. Compact Redis state is reconstructible and is not backed up. Upgrade and uninstall After checking out the reviewed target release: The command creates a checksummed pre upgrade backup, pulls current base images, rebuilds the application images from the checked out release, reapplies migrations, and waits for health. Test restore before upgrading important installations. Remove containers while preserving data and secrets with bun run compact:uninstall . Destructive removal is explicit: The destructive form removes Compact volumes and its generated environment file. Verify an external backup first.

title: Configure services and secrets
description: Validate environment contracts for API, worker, applications, databases, providers, signing, and storage.
body: Start from .env.local.example for local development and your platform's secret manager for deployed environments. Never commit a populated environment file. Validate by mode Use the mode matching the environment. Production checks are intentionally stricter and must not be bypassed with local capture values. Separate public and private values Only variables explicitly designed for public browser use may use a public prefix. Database URLs, provider secrets, webhook secrets, API keys, encryption/signing material, object storage credentials, and Temporal credentials remain server only. Rotate a secret after suspected exposure and restart/redeploy every process that consumes it. Verify old credentials no longer authenticate. Configuration drift Record non secret environment contracts in deployment configuration, validate them before release, and compare API/worker settings that must agree, including database, Temporal namespace/task queue, storage, and provider mode. After every required mode passes, continue to the deployment runbook /self hosting/deployment .

title: Choose and operate a database
description: Use only the database modes covered by Tixkit migrations, repositories, and compatibility validation.
body: PostgreSQL is the default local path. MySQL and MSSQL behavior is limited to the compatibility explicitly exercised by repository migrations and tests. Do not infer support for an untested engine/version from Kysely's general capabilities. Provision safely Use TLS, private networking, a least privilege application identity, bounded connection pools, monitored storage, and automated backups. Keep migration credentials separate when the application identity should not alter schema. Validate compatibility Run the engine specific migration and integration gates documented by the repository before adopting a version or managed service. Test timestamps, JSON, indexes, locking, pagination, unique constraints, and rollback/forward behavior with production like settings. Operational rule Never repair application state by editing production rows without an approved runbook, backup, tenant scope, and verification plan. Prefer supported API, repository, workflow, and compensation paths.

title: Deploy Tixkit
description: Build, migrate, release, smoke-test, and roll back the API, worker, applications, and documentation coherently.
body: Deploy immutable artifacts built from one reviewed commit. The API, worker, OpenAPI reference, SDK compatibility statements, dashboard, checkout, and docs must describe the same contract. Use the Compact profile /self hosting/compact for a complete supported single host evaluation or smaller installation. Use the Production profile and externally operated backing services for high availability and independent scaling. Release order 1. Back up and verify restore readiness. 2. Run the release dry run and documentation/OSS export gates. 3. Apply forward compatible migrations using the approved migration identity. 4. Deploy API and worker with compatible Temporal workflow code. 5. Deploy admin, checkout, and docs. 6. Verify health, representative public/authenticated reads, checkout, workflow, webhook, and documentation routes. Rollback Roll back application artifacts independently only while contract and migration compatibility permits it. Prefer a forward fix for destructive schema changes. Preserve documentation redirects so dashboard links remain valid across a docs rollback. Smoke checks Verify /health for API and docs, worker readiness, a real published test event, authenticated context, and a test safe checkout. A green homepage is not a complete deployment proof. Continue with observability configuration /self hosting/observability before accepting the release.

title: Configure object storage
description: Store uploads and generated artifacts in a private S3-compatible bucket with controlled download paths.
body: Configure endpoint, bucket, region, access key, and secret only on server processes that require storage. Use a least privilege identity restricted to the intended bucket/prefix. Keep the bucket private. Public or authenticated download behavior must flow through the API's documented allowlisted or signed routes; object keys are not authorization. Validate upload, durable read, signed download expiry, public allowlist behavior, deletion/retention, and failure recovery. Monitor capacity, error rate, and credential expiry. Include required artifacts in backup/restore rehearsals rather than assuming database backups are sufficient.

title: Configure observability
description: Monitor request, workflow, datastore, provider, export, checkout, and documentation health without logging sensitive data.
body: Collect service level metrics, traces, structured logs, and health signals for the API, worker, admin, checkout, docs, database, Redis, Temporal, storage, and configured providers. Correlate safely Use request, workflow, delivery, export job, checkout session, and order identifiers only where policy permits. Redact authorization headers, cookies, API keys, signing secrets, provider credentials, ticket codes, and personal data payloads. Alert on outcomes Alert on error/latency saturation, worker/task queue lag, failed checkout finalization, payment reconciliation, webhook dead letters, export failures, database pool pressure, storage errors, and documentation smoke failures. Avoid alerts based only on process uptime. Link alerts to the exact incident runbook /operations/incidents and verify alert routing during release rehearsal.

title: Upgrade Tixkit
description: Rehearse contract, migration, workflow, SDK, documentation, and rollback compatibility before production rollout.
body: Read release and documentation changes for API, SDK, CLI, configuration, providers, migrations, and workflows. Build the sanitized OSS tree and run the release dry run before upgrading. Compact operators check out the reviewed target release and run bun run compact:upgrade . The command creates a pre upgrade backup before rebuilding, migrating, and waiting for the complete profile to become healthy. Rehearse Clone production like data into an isolated environment using the approved sanitization process. Apply migrations, deploy API/worker together where workflow compatibility requires it, then run checkout, order, webhook, export, check in, and docs smoke paths. Roll forward or back Confirm the old application can run against the new schema before treating binary rollback as safe. Preserve Temporal replay compatibility. When rollback is unsafe, use the documented forward repair and restore decision instead of forcing an older binary. Monitor errors, workflow failures, provider outcomes, and database performance through the rollout window.

title: Support and responsible reporting
description: Choose the correct private or public channel for usage questions, defects, security issues, and documentation changes.
body: Use repository discussions or the documented support destination for usage questions that contain no private data. Use issue templates for reproducible public defects and documentation problems. Report security vulnerabilities privately through the process in SECURITY.md ; never open a public issue containing exploit detail, credentials, tenant data, or customer information. For an operational incident, follow incident runbooks /operations/incidents and your organization's escalation policy. Public community support is not a production paging service. When reporting a docs problem, include the canonical page URL, source path, version/commit when known, and the incorrect or missing outcome. Remove secrets, personal data, private topology, and internal payloads.
